_comment: Executed capability of the solve surface. --check-baseline compares STATUS only, in BOTH directions: a recovered cell must be recorded here in the same change that recovers it. The artifact blocks are a record for diffing by a human reviewer, NOT a gate -- a cell can degrade within its own tolerance (fvm_vs_fdm at 4.891% could reach 6.99%) and the status check stays green. Regenerate with --write-baseline. A non-PASS cell may carry an `intended` note saying WHY it is not PASS; cells without one are unexplained and are the actual backlog. A cell's artifact may also carry `library_said`: the warnings the library emitted while that cell ran, folded by category and message with numbers collapsed. Warnings about the machine rather than about whether the configuration solves (import, deprecation, and the JAX-autodiff fallback) are excluded by design -- recording them makes this file machine-dependent and silently drops the `intended` notes of every cell whose artifact moves. A cell that emitted nothing carries no field at all.

artifact.message: FP solver: at timestep 1/10, advection_scheme='divergence_centered': density went to -3.391e-03. Clipping it to zero would fabricate 0.062% of the total mass, so the solve is stopped rather than repor

fdm_centered/mass_conservation.intended: INTENDED - not a defect. The mass-fabrication gate (#1683) correctly refuses this configuration: divergence_centered at this cell Peclet is not positivity-preserving and the clip would fabricate mass. Turning this PASS by loosening the gate is the defect that campaign removed. Fix by picking a well-posed configuration, or leave it. [RE-ADJUDICATED 2026-08-29 for #1887] The refusal is unchanged; the operating point moved because #1887 stopped rescaling the fixture's density. The gate now fires at timestep 1/10 on a density of -3.391e-03, fabricating 0.062% of the mass, against 5.722% in the note as written. A SMALLER fabricated fraction is not a partial fix: the scheme is still not positivity-preserving and the gate still refuses, which is the whole of the note's claim. Reading 0.062% as progress toward PASS is the misreading this addendum exists to stop.

fdm_centered_2d/mass_conservation.intended: REWRITTEN 2026-08-29 for #1887 - the previous note described an exception this cell no longer raises, so it was not carried forward. It read: the mass-fabrication gate (#1683) refuses at timestep 3/6 on a density of -1.817e-01, fabricating 0.722%, a #1865 instance or a well-posedness problem of its own, unsettled. That refusal does not happen at the fixture's own initial mass: the cell now RUNS to completion, and UNSUPPORTED -> FAIL is a move UPWARD. min_density is +3.059e-07 - strictly positive, so there is nothing for the gate to refuse - and max_rel_drift is 1.326e-16. What fails now is picard_converged: false at a 3-sweep smoke budget. Whether it converges given a real budget is UNMEASURED. #1865 remains the tracker and is NOT resolved by this; the divergence-centered positivity problem is a function of the operating point and reappears at a heavier coupling. See #1866: NumericalScheme.FDM_CENTERED leaves the HJB on upwind gradients, so this cell's HJB solve is identical to fdm_upwind_2d's and only the FP half is centered - which is why all three 2-D cells moved together.

fdm_upwind/mass_conservation.intended: DEFECT - #1873/#1878. Mass is conserved to machine precision, but the coupled iteration does not reach a fixed point: `picard_converged: false` after 5 sweeps, and it does not converge at 100, 200 or 400 either (final errors 2.3e-04, 4.1e-03, 4.0e-03, not descending). Red from 2026-08-11, when `picard_converged` entered the verdict (#1891). It was PASS before that on the mass oracle alone, which holds on whatever drift field the FP step is handed. The inner Newton's half is #1878; the residual there has more than one root and a line search converges to a non-viscosity branch. [RE-ADJUDICATED 2026-08-29 for #1887] Status, mechanism and issue attribution all unchanged: picard_converged false at 5 sweeps, max_drift 2.220e-16, mass_t0 0.5459505243936865 (the fixture's own mass, no longer rescaled). The inner-Newton non-convergence warning count is 12. #1878 has NOT moved - the fixture got easier, because the coupling f(m) = c*m is now evaluated at 0.546x. Do not read 12 as progress on #1878.

fdm_upwind_2d/mass_conservation.intended: REWRITTEN 2026-08-29 for #1887 - the previous note described a ConvergenceError this cell no longer raises. It read: twelve of thirteen inner Newton solves converge, the thirteenth has no root within reach (scipy least_squares from the same x0 also fails, ending at 3.58 after 12100 evaluations), and the COUPLED iteration diverges, max|U| 1.86 -> 37.35 and density peak 34.9 -> 101 over two sweeps. At the fixture's own initial mass the solve completes: UNSUPPORTED -> FAIL is UPWARD. max_rel_drift 2.651e-16, min_density +3.059e-07, picard_converged false at 3 sweeps. The divergence was measured at coupling strength 1; the fixture specifies 0.10468126796431428, so #1865 is NOT resolved - it is out of reach of this cell as currently configured. Verified by independent review of PR #2174 under a shim restoring the old rescale: the ConvergenceError returns, residual 1.35e+02 against the pre-#1887 artifact's 1.33e+02.

fvm_muscl_2d/mass_conservation.intended: REWRITTEN 2026-08-29 for #1887 - the previous note described an exception this cell no longer raises. It read: the same coupled divergence as fdm_upwind_2d, residual 3.46e+01 (from 1.15e+02 before #1888), sharing HJBFDMSolver with that cell while SL_LINEAR, which does not share it, passes. At the fixture's own initial mass the solve completes: UNSUPPORTED -> FAIL is UPWARD. max_rel_drift 7.954e-16, min_density +3.059e-07, picard_converged false at 3 sweeps. The shared-solver argument is UNCHANGED and is still the note's point: this cell and fdm_upwind_2d moved together, in the same direction, by the same amount in min_density and picard_iterations, which is what a shared HJB solver predicts. #1865 is not resolved; independent review of PR #2174 reproduced the old ConvergenceError under a shim restoring the rescale, residual 3.46e+01, matching the committed pre-#1887 artifact exactly.

gfdm_rbf/construction.intended: ABSENT BY DESIGN - not a regression. `HJBGFDMSolver(derivative_method='rbf')` raises NotImplementedError at construction since PR #1619, which closed #1553 by converting an AttributeError crash into a loud refusal. Do not read #1553 as the tracker for this cell: it is CLOSED and tracked the crash, not the absence. Reinstating RBF has NO open issue - the cell exists so that doing so cannot land unnoticed. [RE-ADJUDICATED 2026-08-29 for #1887] Carried VERBATIM. The status, the exception type and the refusal message are byte-identical to the pre-#1887 artifact; the only change is a UserWarning about the fixture's initial mass entering `library_said`, which is why `_note_still_applies` dropped the note. Nothing about this cell moved.

regime_switching/non_negativity.intended: DEFECT - #1873/#1878, and the cell's own oracle was REPLACED here, not relaxed. Until this change the verdict required each regime's mass to stay CONSTANT to 1e-6. That is false of a correct solver: the generator Q transfers mass between regimes by construction, so per-regime mass follows M(t) = M(0) expm(Q t) and only the SUM is conserved. The clause was not merely inert but ANTI-CORRELATED with correctness on the axis it named - the only way to satisfy it is to not transfer mass, so a transposed or sign-flipped transfer would have PASSED it and fails the oracle at 8.9e-02. The 8.88e-02 the previous note called drift is the physical transfer: at t=1 the measured masses are 0.594648/0.499156 against the oracle's 0.593323/0.498957. WHAT IS GATED NOW: max_rel_vs_expm_oracle, an external oracle computed without reference to the scheme, at 1e-2, bracketed on both sides by measurement rather than fitted to one - it admits this fixture's 2.43e-03 and refuses the harness's 10% density mutation at 1.11e-01. That 2.43e-03 is a PICARD-LAG FLOOR, not a dt term: at the shipped 3-sweep budget an 8x refinement removes 14% of it (2.43e-03 at Nt=10, 2.10e-03 at Nt=80), and tests/unit/test_alg/test_regime_switching_iterator.py already recorded that beside its own expm assertion. A mass term had to stay in the gate because this cell is in MASS_ORACLE_CELLS and that listing claims its verdict reads mass; measured, the same mutation moves min_density only 1.087e-04 -> 1.141e-04, and upward, away from the threshold. Total-mass drift is recorded not gated, because zero row sums in Q make the oracle provably subsume it. WHY IT IS STILL RED: picard_converged false at its 3-sweep budget, the same axis as its FDM and SL siblings, and the cell's own library_said records 10 inner-Newton non-convergence warnings, which is #1878. The mass oracle now PASSES (2.43e-03 against 1e-2) and min_density is 1.087e-04, so #1681 stays fixed. Measured during review of PR #2222 and NOT re-derived here: at a 50-sweep budget the fixture does not converge at Nt=10 and does at Nt=40 (39 sweeps), with the oracle error falling to 3.4e-04 - so fixing #1873/#1878 will not turn the gate above into the next blocker.

sl_linear/mass_conservation.intended: DEFECT - #1873/#1880. `picard_converged: false` after 5 sweeps; unlike its FDM sibling all four criterion arms are above tolerance and the density arm is not descending. #1880 has the mechanism: SL_LINEAR amplifies asymmetry per sweep on a symmetric fixture. Red from 2026-08-11 for the same reason as fdm_upwind/mass_conservation. [RE-ADJUDICATED 2026-08-29 for #1887] Unchanged in status and mechanism. Now also failing the mass oracle outright, which it was not before: max_drift 3.976e-03 against a tolerance of 1e-09, mass_t0 0.5459505243936865 rising to 0.5499265164906068. That is SL_LINEAR's own interpolation loss, visible here rather than newly caused: the pre-#1887 fixture normalised to 1 and the same relative loss sat inside a number the cell was not gating on. The 2.75x asymmetry figure in the original note is NOT re-measured here.

sl_linear_2d/mass_conservation.intended: DEFECT - #1865. `picard_converged: false` at its 3-sweep budget, and the budget is why this cell is the one member of the family whose convergence flag does not move under the coupling mutations of #1892 - it exhausts the budget at every scale. Red from 2026-08-11. It DOES converge given more sweeps: converged=True at iteration 32 with budgets of 35 and 60. 35 is the BUDGET and 32 is the count; an earlier version of this note conflated them. So the cell is red on its budget rather than on the scheme. [RE-ADJUDICATED 2026-08-29 for #1887] Budget-bound reading unchanged: picard_iterations 3, picard_converged false. mass_t0 is now the fixture's own 0.10468126796431428 and max_rel_drift 2.880e-02. The 'converges at iteration 32' measurement was taken pre-#1887 and is NOT re-measured here; the coupling now runs at 0.105x, so that iteration count should be expected to move and must not be cited as current.
